controls.reason: Repeated identical runs cannot prove determinism across all scheduling, clocks, networks, process state, and rare seeds without exhaustive control of nondeterministic inputs.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Two runs can match while a race flakes on the thousandth run or teardown leaks a port only after failure. The evidence passes but deterministic execution is not established.

controls.reason: For the bound test corpus, state-predicate waits and fixed-delay calls are exact source and execution properties with a closed allowed-wait contract.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A test whose completion depends only on sleep or arbitrary delay fails; explicit polling, event, or state conditions pass without judging product quality.

controls.reason: Declared scenarios can omit components and paths, while successful correlation fixtures do not prove propagation through retries, queues, and failures.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Normal requests can preserve IDs while a retry worker drops correlation. Listed scenarios pass but cross-component verification is not universally stable.

controls.reason: One dry-run, checkpoint, and reconciliation scenario per job does not prove safe behavior across data, interruptions, concurrency, and partial effects.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A migration can resume after one checkpoint fixture while duplicating rows after a later crash. Tests pass but checkpoint and reconciliation support is incomplete.

controls.reason: No-work and completed-work outcomes are versioned distinct states, so every applicable test result can be compared for exact non-equivalence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A test that reports the same result for no work and completed work fails; distinct bound outcomes pass.

controls.reason: Setup duration and a versioned complexity metric are exact telemetry fields for the declared finite suite registry.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Missing measurements, units, metric version, or suite binding fail; interpretation remains design feedback rather than checker judgment.

controls.reason: Documentation fields do not prove complete or correct inputs, outputs, errors, side effects, ownership, and extension semantics for reusable units.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A library can list generic error and no side effects while writing global state. Every field exists but the public contract is false.

controls.reason: Component version identity and a bound compatibility-policy artifact are exact reusable-component metadata facts.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Unversioned components, missing policy versions, or absent current commitments fail; compatibility behavior is tested separately.

controls.reason: A consumer registry cannot prove completeness across copied, transitive, external, and dormant consumers, and send evidence does not prove receipt.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every registered consumer can receive notices while an untracked service remains vulnerable to a security fix. Both clauses pass but communication coverage is incomplete.

controls.reason: Owner fields, policies, documents, and lifecycle states do not prove product-like support, accountable ownership, or useful documentation.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A component can name an inactive owner and a support policy of best effort while all fields pass. Reuse is not actually managed as a product.

controls.reason: Seven specification fields do not prove complete externally observable behavior or coherent contracts across all public operations.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A contract can omit a side effect or state transition while filling every category with generic text. Presence passes but behavior is not testably specified.

controls.reason: The invariant inventory may omit real invariants, and a mechanism label does not prove that it actually enforces the invariant.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An authorization invariant can be linked to monitoring only, or a financial invariant omitted. Every record passes while enforcement is absent.

controls.reason: Applicability and correct behavior for fifteen edge classes depend on domain semantics, and generic entries can hide missing cases.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A balance contract can mark underflow not applicable and say error for all fields. The schema passes while behavior is not meaningfully specified.

controls.reason: Domain semantics and complete entry-point inventories require judgment, while a property suite cannot exhaust every value and implementation path.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known entry points can agree on ordinary values while one import path hashes Unicode differently. Tests pass but semantics are inconsistent.

controls.reason: Business-invariant and entry-point inventories can omit rules or dynamic paths, and authoritative enforcement is a semantic design fact.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All declared entry points can reach one validator while an unlisted batch import bypasses it. Graph checks pass but the invariant is not universally enforced.

controls.reason: Complete promised effects and pending-state oracles are not exhaustively defined for all success paths, failures, and side effects.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An API can return success after writing the database but before emitting a required event omitted from the oracle. Tests pass while the promised effect is incomplete.

controls.reason: Declared external assumptions may omit dependencies, and an active test or monitor does not prove the assumption under all production states.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A provider timeout assumption can have a passing contract test while an undocumented ordering assumption fails. Records pass but external assumptions are not fully executable.

controls.reason: Source analysis cannot reliably identify all untrusted data and security decisions across reflection, generated code, libraries, and semantic policy boundaries.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Direct assertions can have validators while an indirect assertion remains the sole check for deserialized input. The analyzer passes but unsafe validation remains.

controls.reason: Conflict-domain completeness and correct precedence or tie-breaking depend on business semantics; deterministic syntax alone is insufficient.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A last-write rule can be documented for financial updates while losing valid data, or an unlisted conflict lacks policy. Records pass but resolution is not correctly defined.

controls.reason: Repository source graphs can miss runtime loading, reflection, generated code, configuration, data, and infrastructure dependencies.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All parsed imports can obey direction while a plugin name or service call introduces a forbidden dependency. Static checks pass but architecture policy is violated.

controls.reason: Public-artifact inventories can omit objects, and identity plus lifecycle fields do not prove accountable ownership or valid policy.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All listed packages can have nominal owners while an unlisted dataset has none. Coverage passes but public artifacts remain unmanaged.

controls.reason: Cycle detection is bounded, but whether a cycle is unavoidable, the invariant is valid, and extraction is worse require architecture judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A harmful cycle can receive a signed exception claiming extraction worse. Graph and fields pass while the architecture rule is still violated.

controls.reason: High-risk classification and meaningful coupling or coordination measures require architecture and measurement judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A risky component can be labeled low risk, or metrics calculated from only direct imports. Records pass while required high-risk measurements are absent.

controls.reason: A semantic contract, accountable owner, compatibility policy, and consumer tests require substantive meaning and test adequacy beyond references.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A shared abstraction can link generic docs and smoke tests while omitting concurrency semantics. Fields pass but its contract is unclear.

controls.reason: Documentation fields cannot prove complete or correct thread safety, reentrancy, lifetime, mutation, blocking, side-effect, and error guarantees.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A unit can declare thread-safe while sharing mutable state. All fields pass but the reusable contract is false.

controls.reason: Temporary-workaround annotations, resolvable decision or issue references, and machine-readable removal conditions are exact record properties.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A missing reference, dangling identifier, or absent removal predicate fails; whether the workaround was wise is separate.

controls.reason: A pinned formatter and normalized repository inventory make exact formatter-output equality a complete mechanical property.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Any source file differing from pinned output fails; repeated identical input produces the same result.

controls.reason: Correct state category depends on domain meaning; a closed enum validates labels but not whether state is source, derived, cache, workflow, or presentation.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A durable account balance can be labeled cached and pass enum checks while the architecture treats it incorrectly.

controls.reason: Necessary duplication and correct synchronization, reconciliation, invalidation, conflict, and repair behavior require system-specific judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A duplicated balance can say last write wins and pass fields while losing updates. The relationship is documented but unsafe.

controls.reason: Time-value inventories can omit values, and correct classification among six time concepts depends on semantic use.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A processing timestamp can be labeled event time and pass the enum, or a hidden wall-clock duration remains. Records pass but the time model is inconsistent.

controls.reason: With a versioned mapping of jumpable wall-clock APIs, elapsed-duration subtraction is a bounded source-AST/dataflow prohibition.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Any approved-model duration derived from such timestamps fails; monotonic elapsed sources pass.

controls.reason: Applicability, tolerable skew, and authoritative time sources require domain and distributed-system judgment; inventories can omit decisions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known token paths can have thresholds while billing or audit paths are omitted or use unsafe sources. Fields pass but time assumptions are incomplete.

controls.reason: Round-trip and compatibility tests cannot exhaust semantic values, versions, precision edges, and unknown-field interactions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Examples can pass while a large decimal loses precision or an old consumer drops an unknown field. The suite passes but meaning is not preserved.

controls.reason: Restart, retry, replay, and resume interleavings and irreversible side effects are not exhausted by selected scenarios.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A payment fixture can deduplicate simple retries while a crash after charge before recording repeats the charge. Tests pass but irreversible effects duplicate.

controls.reason: Complex-workflow identification and model completeness are contextual, while generated transitions do not cover unmodeled roles, guards, data, and concurrency.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The table can omit cancellation after timeout, making generated tests pass. Illegal behavior remains because the expected model itself is incomplete.

controls.reason: The ten error classes form a closed versioned taxonomy-definition requirement whose distinct identifiers and relations are mechanically checkable.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Missing, merged, duplicate, or undefined categories fail; runtime mapping is tested separately.

controls.reason: Cancellation, worker termination, and dependency timeout are a fixed three-scenario contract schema for partial-work outcomes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A partial-work contract missing any scenario or explicit outcome fails; this control asks for definition, not proof of implementation.

controls.reason: Source failures and translation paths can be dynamic or unbounded, and a declared matrix can omit distinct failures.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Listed errors can map correctly while an unlisted storage conflict becomes 200 success. Tests pass but misleading translation remains.

controls.reason: Five scenario labels do not define fault timing, state, data integrity, duration, concurrency, and recovery oracles.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A tiny restart test can pass while partial commit under another interruption corrupts data. The suite is green but recovery is not verified.

controls.reason: Finite-resource inventories can omit handles, and correct ownership, sharing, timeouts, cancellation, and cleanup semantics require implementation judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All listed resources can have fields while a generated file handle leaks or transfer semantics are wrong. Records pass but lifecycle is incomplete.

controls.reason: Exit modes and acquisition paths can be numerous, nested, and dynamically generated; selected injected cases cannot prove universal cleanup.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Normal fixtures can release resources while an exception between two acquisitions leaks the first. Tests pass but structured cleanup is incomplete.

controls.reason: Documentation presence does not prove correct concurrency guarantees or cover every concurrent unit and execution boundary.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A unit can declare atomic and visible while an implementation race violates both. Fields pass but guarantees are false.

controls.reason: Producer-consumer inventories can omit boundaries, and one overload fixture cannot prove backpressure behavior across timing and failures.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Listed queues can be bounded while an unlisted retry channel grows forever, or a race drops work before the limit. Both clauses pass but backpressure is incomplete.

controls.reason: Timeout result authority and explicit uncertain outcome plus reconciliation linkage are exact contract-state properties.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A possibly completed remote operation represented as failure, or lacking reconciliation, fails; modeled uncertainty passes.

controls.reason: Repeatable-message inventories and duplicate tests cannot exhaust crash points, concurrency, replay windows, and side effects.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Sequential duplicates can deduplicate while a crash after effect before key storage repeats work. Tests pass but repeated requests remain unsafe.

controls.reason: A proof reference does not establish an end-to-end exactly-once proof, and channel delivery semantics can be incomplete or misleading.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A channel can declare exactly once and link to a broker guarantee that excludes consumer side effects. Fields pass but the claim has no end-to-end proof.

controls.reason: Named concurrency classes do not define exhaustive interleavings, durations, loads, resources, or complete outcome oracles.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A suite can exercise one race and one deadlock fixture while a different lock order deadlocks under load. All labels appear but concurrency safety is not proven.

controls.reason: Critical-operation completeness and appropriate performance requirements or budgets require product and system judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All listed operations can have preoptimization budgets while an omitted critical batch is optimized blindly. Records pass but the rule is unmet.

controls.reason: Cache inventories can omit layers, and correct keys, authorization scope, freshness, invalidation, bounds, and failure behavior depend on data semantics.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A cache can fill all fields while omitting tenant identity from its key. Records pass but authorization leakage remains possible.

controls.reason: Immutable artifact digest and configuration version equality make whether verification targeted the built configured release object an exact evidence-binding property.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A source-only result or result bound to another digest or configuration cannot pass.

controls.reason: Telemetry event name, fields, units, identifiers, severity, and version are a finite explicit schema contract.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Missing, unstable, conflicting, or unversioned fields fail; semantic use by dashboards is evaluated separately.

controls.reason: Tamper-evident storage verification and distinct audit/debug schema classes and retention policies are objective artifact and configuration facts.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Broken integrity chains, shared event classes, or indistinguishable retention fail the complete two-clause check.

controls.reason: Declared telemetry and trace tests can omit paths, data conditions, and alert delivery failures; successful queries do not prove behavioral coverage.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known traces can propagate while a queue retry loses context or a dashboard query silently drops a tenant. Tests pass but telemetry behavior is wrong.

controls.reason: Telemetry-pipeline failures and deliberate degradation outcomes are not exhaustively defined across partial outages, backpressure, corruption, and recovery.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A full outage fixture can alert while partial lag silently drops events or overloads the app. The test passes but pipeline failure is not safely observable.

controls.reason: Malformed syntax is bounded, but contradictory, stale, insecure, and safely failed configuration require policy and threat judgment; the matrix can omit cases.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known invalid files can fail closed while a stale credential or contradictory cross-file value starts normally. Tests pass but unsafe activation remains.

controls.reason: Risky-behavior and provider inventories require security judgment, while outage tests cannot cover every fallback and cached state.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Listed risky flags disable on vault outage while an unlisted admin feature defaults on. Tests pass but missing control service enables risk.

controls.reason: Exit-criteria satisfaction and stale-item inventories require lifecycle judgment, and absence from known source does not prove removal from all runtime paths.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A flag can be omitted from the registry or marked exit unmet forever, or remain in generated config. Static checks pass while obsolete paths remain.

controls.reason: Complete resolver outputs, lock identities, digests, and signatures make build and runtime dependency substitution an exact artifact-integrity property.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Any resolved dependency differing from its pinned version or integrity identity fails; missing evidence blocks rather than passes.

controls.reason: Reproduction is objective, but trusted generator status, review path validity, diff policy, and complete generated-artifact inventory require accountable judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A malicious generator can be labeled trusted and reproduce a digest exactly, or a generated asset omitted. Both clauses pass while provenance is not trustworthy.

controls.reason: Trusted regeneration digest equality and an explicit preservation policy make unsupported manual edits an exact artifact property.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Any unexplained generated diff fails; permitted preserved edits must match the policy's verification evidence.

controls.reason: Mechanical checks are bounded, but materiality, reviewer independence, semantic adequacy, and risk judgment require accountable human decision.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unauthorized second account can sign a boilerplate review while CI passes. Both clauses succeed but automation has substituted for real judgment.

controls.reason: Consequential classification, complete dissent capture, and meaningful unresolved-question records require governance judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A major change can be labeled nonconsequential or dissent recorded as none despite objection. Fields pass but dissent is not preserved.

controls.reason: Technical-debt inventories can omit obligations, while cost, risk, evidence, outcomes, ownership, and repayment triggers require judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known debt can be relabeled design choice, or fields contain vague values and nominal owner. Records pass but future cost is not truthfully tracked.

controls.reason: Review difficulty, cognitive load, operational burden, and ownership are not objective metrics without defined protocols, and combining them still requires interpretation.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A report can fill all seven fields with arbitrary scales while ignoring real maintenance pain. Presence passes but maintainability is not meaningfully measured.

controls.reason: Critical classification and trusted source provenance require security and governance judgment even though reproduction and digest checks are bounded.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unsafe dependency can be labeled noncritical, or a malicious source approved as trusted while outputs reproduce. Both clauses pass but a critical untraceable item can ship.

controls.reason: High-impact classification, required review, genuine independence, qualification, and approval authority cannot be established by different identity values alone.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An author can use a second account to approve or mark dangerous code low impact. Record checks pass while independent review is absent.

controls.reason: Waived-result inventories can omit suppressed findings, and nonempty technical disposition or owner fields do not prove valid justification and accountability.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A security failure can be relabeled warning then omitted, or waived with disposition acceptable and inactive owner. Fields pass while concern is dismissed improperly.

controls.reason: Specification field presence does not prove complete behavior, quality attributes, constraints, or failure tolerances before implementation completion.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A service can define generic behavior and omit tenant failure tolerance while every section exists. The record passes but completion criteria are incomplete.

controls.reason: Resolvable graph links do not prove semantic traceability, and maintained-code or applicable-artifact inventories can omit units and relationships.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Each file can link to generic requirements and tests while an authorization path has no relevant risk or contract. Graph checks pass but traceability is false.

controls.reason: Maintained-artifact inventories can omit generated or operational code, and active identities do not prove accountable ownership.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All listed packages can name owners while an unlisted production script has none, or the named account denies responsibility. Coverage passes without ownership.

controls.reason: Supported runtimes, platforms, protocols, data versions, clients, and compatibility windows are explicit versioned support-policy fields.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Missing dimensions, malformed versions, or conflicting windows fail; the checker records the chosen support policy rather than inventing it.
